newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy deputy PM urges unions to help on pensions.
newsitem.headline: Italy deputy PM urges unions to help on pensions.

text.p: Italy's Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni on Thursday called on the unions to help reform the pensions system.
"We have to get on with a reform of the pensions system," Veltroni said in a speech to a congress of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), the biggest in the centre-left government.
"I hope the discussion with unions is intense and sincere," he added.
Italy's powerful union leaders have said they would be opposed to any cuts in social spending.
Italy carried out a landmark reform of the pension system in 1995 and its effects are due to be studied in 1998.
The government wants to conduct a wide-ranging reform of the welfare state. But Veltroni said the left was not seeking "cuts to the welfare state but a fairer welfare state".
Veltroni said: "Either the entire left has the courage to take this great reform in hand or...the real processes will sweep it away."
Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi has urged the government to carry out a major reform of the welfare state.
